source.title: Remote Sensing Semantic Segregation for Water Information Extraction: Optimization of Samples via Training Error Performance
source.authors: Rui Wang; Yizhuo Meng; Wen Zhang; Ziyao Li; Fengmin Hu; Lingkui Meng

record.tranche_reason: Tests how filtering suspected corrupted training samples affects held-out accuracy in remote-sensing water segmentation, a new setting for the claim's generalization topic.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fitting random labels but does not test random-label fitting or chance-level test performance. It reports held-out performance after filtering suspected corrupted samples; these results do not test any listed version's specific behavior.
record.test_reason: The study uses neural-network memorization capacity to motivate filtering suspected corrupted labels and evaluates its filtering method. It does not test any listed version. In particular, loss-based corruption ranking is not V8's inclusion-based memorization measure, and there is no equal-sized random-removal control.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their sample-filtering method improves prediction accuracy and training stability. They acknowledge that corrupted information remains and that intervention timing and optimization count require manual settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study filters suspected corrupted samples during mini-batch gradient descent training; it does not reproduce a listed version's method.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention starts at a preset threshold of approximately 9700; each optimization removes the top 40% of suspected corrupted data, and the process is repeated 3 times.

fits_no_version.finding: Filtering suspected corrupted samples improves FCN held-out accuracy relative to unfiltered training at the same iteration count, according to Section IV-C and Figure 20(c).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time filtering based on loss-derived corruption scores can improve held-out water-segmentation accuracy on GF-1 imagery.

record.problems: Exact held-out accuracy values are presented only in figures; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The held-out set consists of manually screened accurate data from the same water-segmentation task.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant held-out result with a recoverable, separately stated value was reported. Training-error and loss-distribution results do not directly measure the listed versions' outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing examples ranked by inclusion-based memorization, compared with equal-sized random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The improvement from removing suspected corrupted labels neither supports nor challenges V8. The selection criterion, comparison group, and intervention differ from that version. Comparisons among convolutional segmentation architectures also do not test V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error changes.
Comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removal of examples identified by their memorization effect and comparison with random removal.

rows.subject: FCN
rows.operation_detail: Repeatedly removes the top 40% of samples ranked as suspected corrupted data; compares optimized and unoptimized training.

conditions.value: 2972 pairs of accurate, manually screened data

rows.note: The text states that the optimized model had higher ability to express water information and that data-optimized training produced better model accuracy for the same number of iterations. Exact values are shown only in figures.
rows.check: The reported accuracy improvement does not measure any listed version. Figure 20(c) supports a qualitative held-out improvement, but numerical values are unavailable in the supplied text. Figure 19 concerns a sample participating in training and should not be cited as held-out evidence. This row compares the study's filtering method with unfiltered training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
